reviewed_candidates.reason: Only proposal and list tools auto-approve in unattended sessions. Mutations never auto-approve unattended, interactive mutations require High autonomy, deletion still requires an explicit permission decision, and direct MCP creation independently enforces High autonomy.
MCP registration and permission recognition share case- and separator-normalized server-name matching, preventing a configured lookalike server from inheriting automation trust.

Automation mutation grants include a bounded stable digest of the mutation arguments, so an Always allow decision for one target or payload does not authorize unrelated automation mutations, while secret-like values are omitted from the stored signature.
Renderer mutation commands use sendIfConnected and reject immediately while disconnected, so create, update, delete, enable, run-now, and confirmation commands cannot be replayed after reconnect.

Worktree names are sanitized, Git is invoked with array arguments, the target must remain lexically inside the selected repository, and every existing target path component is rejected if it is a symbolic link or non-directory.

Cleanup resolves the registered worktrees from Git metadata, accepts only a canonical linked worktree in DROIDEX's .worktrees/<run>/<repository> layout beneath another registered checkout, refuses main and unrelated linked worktrees, refuses dirty worktrees, and uses git worktree remove without force. Cleanup failures are reported rather than falling back to recursive deletion.

Stored definitions, run snapshots, schedules, reasoning levels, and autonomy values are parsed and normalized before use; unknown schema versions are refused and unreadable stores are quarantined rather than executed.
Agent-facing MCP inputs use Zod length and range limits, cron strings are bounded, snapshots and histories are trimmed, and scheduler/run timers have bounded queues and retry intervals.

notes: Pre-existing codebase risks documented in .factory/threat-model.md were not counted unless PR #128 introduced or materially worsened them.
The scan covered the complete origin/main comparison plus eight untracked files in the working tree.
A persisted-path cleanup candidate found during this scan was fixed before the report was finalized; no open vulnerability remains.
